flashcards.front: Why is Hybrid Fan-Out preferred over pure Fan-Out-on-Write for Twitter/X?
flashcards.back: Pushing a single tweet from a 50M-follower celebrity into 50M Redis timelines causes minutes-long queue lag and massive write amplification. Hybrid pushes normal users and merges celebrity posts on read.

quizzes.scenario: Your social app uses pure fan-out on write. When an account with 45 million followers posts, ordinary users wait 12 minutes to see their friends' posts.
quizzes.question: What caused the delay, and what is the usual fix?
options: Feed reads use OFFSET pagination; switch to cursor paging
The 45M-entry fan-out floods the queue; pull big accounts at read time
Fan-out workers lack capacity; autoscale them on queue depth
Timeline cache TTLs are too short; cache feeds for longer
quizzes.explanation: Fan-out on write pushes one timeline entry per follower, so a 45-million-follower post floods the fan-out queue and delays everyone else. Hybrid fan-out skips the push for very large accounts and merges their recent posts in at read time.
optionExplanations: Cursor paging speeds deep reads, but the delay comes from the write fan-out.
Correct. Hybrid fan-out removes the giant write burst.
Autoscaling helps, but each celebrity post still costs 45M writes.
Longer TTLs keep stale feeds; they do not shrink a 45M-entry burst.
